dn17:1.3.9: In the same way, the royal capital of Kusāvatī was successful and prosperous, populous and full of people, with plenty of food.
dn17:1.6.12: In the same way, when those rows of palm trees were blown by the wind they sounded graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, lovely, and intoxicating.
dn17:1.21.3: In the same way, King Mahāsudassana was dear and beloved to the brahmins and householders.
dn17:1.21.6: In the same way, the brahmins and householders were dear and beloved to King Mahāsudassana.
dn17:1.23.11: Those in need of food, drink, clothes, vehicles, beds, women, coined gold, or uncoined gold got what they needed.
dn17:1.29.6: In the same way, when those nets of bells were blown by the wind they sounded graceful, tantalizing, sensuous, lovely, and intoxicating.
dn17:1.29.10: In the same way, the Palace of Principle was hard to look at, dazzling to the eyes.

dn17:2.6.5: ‘Dear commander-treasure, these 84,000 royal elephants of mine come to attend on me at daybreak and dusk. Well then, let 42,000 elephants at a time come to attend on me, once at the end of each century.’
dn17:2.6.6: ‘Yes, Your Majesty,’ replied the commander-treasure to King Mahāsudassana.
dn17:2.6.7: Then, some time later, 42,000 of King Mahāsudassana’s elephants at a time came to attend on him, once at the end of each century.
dn17:2.10.6: Arouse desire for these! Take an interest in life!
dn17:2.10.7: Your Majesty, you have 84,000 chambers, with the Chamber of the Grand Tower foremost.
dn17:2.10.8: Arouse desire for these! Take an interest in life!
